tagline: A woodland circle near Harpers Crossroads carries a tale of the devil.
intro: Devil’s Tramping Ground Road belongs to North Carolina’s scenic-byway network. Its Chatham County setting is gently rolling Piedmont country, with higher hills rising above the general terrain. NCDOT describes its byways as alternatives to the faster traffic and commercial areas of major highways.

Near Harpers Crossroads, a forest clearing called the Devil’s Tramping Ground has inspired persistent local legends. Journalist John William Harden described the story told by Chatham residents: the devil paces the bare circle while devising trouble for humanity.

Pittsboro’s courthouse occupies a traffic circle at the center of town. Farther along the journey, Harpers Crossroads marks the meeting of NC 902 and Siler City Glendon Road. The woodland circle lies near this crossroads in the Bear Creek area.

moments.title: Pittsboro
moments.text: Pittsboro’s town plan began with a land problem. In 1787, the legislature ruled out establishing a town on Mial Scurlock’s property, where the courthouse had been built. The trustees bought adjoining land from William Petty and laid out the town there; Pittsboro officially became the county seat that year. Its name honors William Pitt the Younger, while Chatham County honors his father. The town was considered for both the state university and the state capital. As county seat, it became a center for trade and local government, drawing farmers into town on weekends to do business.

moments.title: Chatham County Courthouse
moments.text: A three-stage cupola rises above the Chatham County Courthouse’s two-story classical portico. Built in 1881, the rectangular brick courthouse stands in the traffic circle at Pittsboro’s center. The Works Progress Administration added a one-story extension in the 1930s, and extensive renovations followed in 1959. The courthouse entered the National Register of Historic Places in 1979. A fire during renovation badly damaged the building in March 2010. The restored courthouse reopened in April 2013, with a county-history exhibit downstairs and a courtroom upstairs.
moments.notice: The portico rises two stories beneath a three-stage cupola.

moments.title: Devil's Tramping Ground
moments.text: The Devil’s Tramping Ground is a woodland circle near Harpers Crossroads whose reputation rests on local lore. Journalist and author John William Harden recorded Chatham residents’ story of the devil walking in circles here while thinking up ways to cause trouble for humanity. In Harden’s telling, that pacing takes place on the bare circle during the night. The place also appears in Poppy Z. Brite’s horror novels Lost Souls and Drawing Blood. Both novels are set at least partly in Missing Mile, a fictional North Carolina city. The real place is also called Devil’s Stomping Ground.
